about: Plate marks for the Prusa CORE One's camera on 2026-11-27, in pixels of its 1920x1080 stream. The calibration plate from tools/camera-calibration (250 x 220 mm) was printed as one 0.2 mm layer with a 0.6 mm nozzle and left on the sheet, and one frame was taken at each of five bed heights, `zc_mm` being the Z the printer read back (M114) for that frame. Every point lies on the outer edge of one of the plate's nine marks, as one `first` curve per frame; the back-right corner mark is above the frame's top edge at the two lowest heights and only partly in it at 30 mm, so it is marked at 45 and 60 mm. The points were placed by sampling each mark's planned outer wall every 3 mm, projecting the samples through a working fit, fitting a small affine of each mark's projected outline to the dark print around it, and moving each sample along the edge's normal, at most 3 px, to the strongest dark-to-bright edge, with a contrast test against the marks' own texture. The landmarks are fixed chassis features: the screws and the label right of the front-right Z leadscrew, the dark bracket's corner at the top right, and the powder-coated edge left of the bed's front. None of them moves with the bed or the gantry, though the gantry hides the top-right one while it passes.
